hook: SCP-112 is a roller coaster whose ride lasts three minutes from the outside and anywhere up to months from the inside. The experiment logs are only the setup; the two interviews at the end are the real payload. They include self-harm, starvation, a crude sexual remark and an attack.
whyItMatters:
The article takes a familiar time-dilation idea and grounds it in the body: hunger, sleeplessness and soreness that the rider remembers in full but never physically suffered. Small procedural details such as keeping a portable toilet and a snack table by the track make the premise feel tested rather than described.

It also shows how much a paired interview can do. Two people sitting side by side on the same physical train, telling stories that cannot both be the same ride, carry the file further than any description could.
thingsToNotice:
The key is that every rider gets a different ride. The former coaster designer had a few great minutes with twists she half remembered sketching herself, while the man beside her spent what seems to be months strapped in next to someone who never once reacted to him. He screamed until his voice gave out, starved, soiled himself and beat his head bloody, all while she kept cheering; from her side, he just slouched there staring ahead.

The ending turns on a single friendly glance. When the ride stops, she finally looks at him, smiles and says something pleasant, and he attacks her trying to get an answer to why. His second interview, done in writing because talking hurts, collapses into a single word repeated until he is stopped, and the doctor's flat note that monthly terminations are coming makes his recovery feel beside the point.
